# ESPN streaming plans are getting more expensive

Starting September 17th, a subscription to ESPN Unlimited will cost $31.99 per month.

Starting September 17th, a subscription to ESPN Unlimited will cost $31.99 per month.

by Emma Roth

Aug 24, 2026, 3:06 PM UTC

Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge

Emma Roth

is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

ESPN is hiking the price of its subscription on September 17th, a change that will also impact its bundles with Disney Plus. In a support page spotted earlier by Sports Media Watch, ESPN says its ad-supported Select membership will cost $13.99 instead of $12.99 / month, while its Unlimited plan will rise to $31.99 from $29.99 / month.

The annual ESPN Select plan is also going to $139.99 from $129.99 / year, and the annual Unlimited tier is increasing to $319.99 from $299.99 / year. Meanwhile, Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Select are going up in price as well. Here’s a rundown of the changes:

- Disney Plus (with ads), Hulu (with ads), and ESPN Select: $21.99 / month, up from $19.99 / month. 
- Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), ESPN Select: $32.99 / month, up from $29.99.
- Legacy Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), and ESPN Select: $27.99 / month, up from $24.99 / month.

Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Unlimited aren’t affected. Last week, Axios reported that about 80 percent of Unlimited subscribers signed up through the bundle with Disney Plus and Hulu.

Though Disney last raised prices across its bundles last year, this is the first increase for ESPN, which rolled out its standalone streaming subscription last August. As part of the launch, ESPN updated its mobile app with a TikTok-like feed of videos and a personalized version of SportsCenter. ESPN also launched multiview in its app on major smart TV platforms.

# What is the new ESPN DTC service? Plans, costs, key facts

ESPN

- ESPN

Aug 21, 2026, 12:30 AM

ESPN launched a direct-to-consumer service in August 2025. The service offers major enhancements within ESPN's streaming and app experiences. Here are key facts to know:

New streaming plan details

When did ESPN direct-to-consumer launch?

The service brought the full suite of ESPN networks and services directly to fans in August 2025.

How can I subscribe to ESPN direct-to-consumer?

Fans can sign up for the new service here.

What plans does ESPN direct-to-consumer offer?

Fans can choose from two plans:

ESPN Unlimited Plan

- Access to all of ESPN's linear networks -- ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network -- in addition to ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+ and ACCNX
- 47,000 live events a year, on demand replays, studio shows, original programming and more

ESPN Select Plan

- Access to all content available on ESPN+
- More than 32,000 live sports events annually, a robust library of exclusive studio shows, on-demand replays, acclaimed original content and more

How much does each plan cost?

ESPN Unlimited Plan: $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year

ESPN Select Plan: $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year

What is available only on the ESPN Unlimited Plan vs. the ESPN Select Plan?

ESPN Unlimited Plan subscribers have access to all ESPN networks, including ESPN+, with events like NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, tennis and golf majors, top-tier college football and basketball, WWE and postseason coverage from all those and more.

ESPN Select Plan subscribers have access only to ESPN+, with top-tier soccer, PGA Tour, NHL, UFC and a selection of college sports, tennis, PLL, UFL and other leagues.

Do you get access to ESPN Unlimited as part of your pay-TV package?

Customers with Hulu + Live TV, DIRECTV, Fubo TV, Spectrum TV, Verizon FiOS, U-verse, Cox, Comcast Xfinity, and other supported providers may already get ESPN Unlimited as part of their pay-TV package, with more partners to come. To activate your ESPN plan or to learn more, please visit the ESPN Fan Support Activation FAQ.

Do both plans include advertising?

Like linear television, both plans have ads during live events and studio shows. Bundle options with Disney+ and Hulu will be available with or without ads on those platforms.

New app plan details

How does ESPN direct-to-consumer impact the overall ESPN app experience?

The enhanced ESPN app integrates game stats, betting information, fantasy sports, commerce, multiview options and a personalized SportsCenter For You. The new features and functionality are available to all fans who watch sports on the ESPN App, whether they subscribe directly or through pay-TV.

If I already use the existing ESPN App, do I need to download anything else with ESPN direct-to-consumer?

All features are available within the existing ESPN App on mobile devices and connected TV.

Impact of ESPN direct-to-consumer on existing plans

If I am an ESPN+ subscriber, do I still have access to the same content?

ESPN+ will continue to be available in a variety of ways. Existing ESPN+ subscribers will become subscribers to the ESPN Select Plan.

How does ESPN direct-to-consumer impact existing Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ bundle subscribers?

Existing Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ bundle subscribers will become subscribers to a Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ Select bundle and continue to receive the same content through the ESPN and Disney+ apps.

Can subscribers still get ESPN via cable bundles with direct-to-consumer?

ESPN will continue to be distributed via pay-TV providers. Pay TV subscribers will have access to the enhanced features within the ESPN App via their pay-TV subscriptions.

# ESPN Unlimited Price Increase: New Prices Start Sept. 17, 2026

August 24, 2026

Written By: 

Jim Kimble

 

ESPN is raising the price of its direct-to-consumer streaming plans just as the college football season gets underway.

Starting Sept. 17, ESPN Unlimited will increase from $29.99 to $31.99 per month, while ESPN Select will rise from $12.99 to $13.99 per month. Annual prices are also going up, with Unlimited increasing from $299.99 to $319.99 and Select moving from $129.99 to $139.99.

The current prices remain in effect through Sept. 16.

For college football fans, the increase makes it more important to look closely at how much ESPN coverage you actually need. 

Sling Essentials still offers ESPN and ESPN2 for $19.99 per month, and you can add Sports Extra to the Essentials plan for $30.99. But you will be missing games on ABC, and SEC Network Plus if you go that route. 

ESPN Unlimited includes the broader ESPN lineup with ESPNU, SEC Network and ACC Network.

Regardless of which teams or conferences you watch, a TV antenna can cover a large share of college football on local ABC, CBS, FOX, CW and NBC stations. A smaller streaming plan plus an antenna is one way to keep the paid portion of your sports lineup cheaper as prices continue to rise.

## ESPN Unlimited and Select Prices Increase Sept. 17

ESPN’s price increase affects both its Unlimited and Select plans, including monthly and annual subscriptions.

| ESPN plan | Current price | Price starting Sept. 17 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ESPN Select monthly | $12.99 | $13.99 |
| ESPN Select annual | $129.99 | $139.99 |
| ESPN Unlimited monthly | $29.99 | $31.99 |
| ESPN Unlimited annual | $299.99 | $319.99 |

The monthly increase is $1 for ESPN Select and $2 for ESPN Unlimited. Annual subscribers will pay $10 more for Select and $20 more for Unlimited.

ESPN Unlimited includes the live ESPN channel lineup, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPNEWS and ESPN Deportes. It also includes the live events and on-demand programming available through ESPN Select.

ESPN Select, formerly ESPN+, is the smaller streaming plan. It carries its own live sports and on-demand programming, but it does not include the live ESPN, ESPN2 or other ESPN cable channels.

Subscribers will pay the current rate through Sept. 16, with the higher price taking effect Sept. 17. 

## What Does the ESPN Price Increase Mean for College Football Fans?

ESPN’s channels carry a large share of the college football schedule.

The price increase does not change what is included with Unlimited. It simply raises the monthly cost from $29.99 to $31.99 starting Sept. 17.

ESPN Unlimited includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SEC Network and ACC Network, along with digital-only feeds such as SEC Network+ and ACC Network Extra. That gives subscribers access to games from several conferences without requiring a TV provider or larger live TV package.

## Cheaper Ways to Watch ESPN Channels

There is a cheaper way to get some ESPN channels. Sling Essentials costs $19.99 per month and includes ESPN and ESPN2. 

Sling Passes can also get you access to some ESPN channels offered through the Orange plan and Sports Extra such as ESPNU, SEC Network or ACC Network. 

ESPN Unlimited still carries exclusive live sports through digital-only channels like ESPN+, and other live sports like the PGA Tour on ESPN Select.

# ESPN Unlimited Plan Explained: What’s Included & How To Get It

by Explore Disney+ Contributor

June 23, 2026

See how much it costs, how it compares to the ESPN Select plan, bundle options, and how to subscribe

Choosing a streaming plan should be easier than keeping up with your favorite teams. The ESPN Unlimited Plan gives fans access to ESPN’s full lineup of networks and services, whether the day calls for a marquee matchup, a studio show, or a documentary about one of sports’ biggest moments.

Before you pick a plan, here’s a quick rundown on who the ESPN Unlimited plan is best for, how it compares with other ESPN options, and what to know if you’re deciding between Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN bundle plans.

## What is the ESPN Unlimited Plan?

The ESPN Unlimited plan is a streaming subscription that gives fans access to the full ESPN lineup. That includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network+, ACC Network Extra, ESPN+, and now NFL Network.

It’s made for fans who want live games, ESPN studio shows, documentaries, replays, and more in one place, especially those without a traditional TV package.

## What’s included with the ESPN Unlimited plan?

With the ESPN Unlimited plan, you can stream all of ESPN’s live linear networks, NFL Network, and ESPN+, SECN+, and ACCNX content through a single subscription. That means access to thousands of live events, studio shows like SportsCenter, on-demand programming, ESPN Originals, and the 30 for 30 library.

Availability can vary by event, location, and league rules, so it’s a good idea to check the ESPN app before game time.

## How much does the ESPN Unlimited plan cost?

The subscription is available for $29.99 per month or $299.99 per year.

## How does ESPN Unlimited compare to ESPN Select?

ESPN Select gives you access to ESPN+ content. ESPN Unlimited builds on ESPN Select by adding live access to all of ESPN’s networks and services.

So, if you want ESPN, ESPN2, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network, ACC Network, NFL Network, ESPN+, and more under one subscription, ESPN Unlimited is the plan for you.

## Can I bundle the ESPN Unlimited plan with Disney+ and Hulu?

Yes. You can get the ESPN Unlimited plan as part of the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle, starting at $35.99 per month.

That means you can combine the ESPN Unlimited plan with Disney+ and Hulu in one subscription, making it the perfect option for households with sports fans, movie watchers, and TV lovers.*

## How can you get the ESPN Unlimited plan?

You can get the ESPN Unlimited plan with a Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle. Once your subscription is active, open the ESPN hub on Disney+ to browse sports, teams, leagues, and tournaments.

You can also subscribe to the ESPN Unlimited plan through the ESPN app. Create an account or log in with your MyDisney account and choose the ESPN Unlimited plan.

The ESPN Unlimited plan includes live coverage across major leagues and events, including NFL, NHL, MLB, WWE, tennis and golf majors, and postseason matchups like the College Football Playoff. Basketball fans can also watch select NBA, WNBA, and college basketball games.

# ESPN to increase price of ESPN Unlimited

> The direct-to-consumer streaming service will now run users $31.99 per month. 

 By Drew Lerner on 08/23/2026 08/23/2026 

Just about one year after its launch, ESPN is raising the price of its direct-to-consumer app.

The price of ESPN Unlimited, the all-encompassing tier of the network’s app that includes access to live linear television feeds across the ESPN family of networks, will increase from $29.99 to $31.99 per month beginning September 17, according to the company’s support page. The news was first noted by Jon Lewis in Sports Media Watch.

Annual subscriptions will also increase. The full-year plan of ESPN Unlimited will now cost $319.99, up $20 from its launch price of $299.99 last August. ESPN Select, the rebranded version of ESPN+ that does not include the flagship ESPN channels, will also see its price increase from $12.99 to $13.99 per month, with the annual subscription also being bumped up by $10.

Lewis reports that those subscribing to ESPN Unlimited through the Disney+ and Hulu bundle will not see a price increase. That bundle will remain priced at $36 per month. According to a recent report by Sara Fischer in Axios, about four in five ESPN Unlimited subscribers are subscribed to that bundle.

It is unclear whether ESPN’s pricing change will impact its other bundle deals with Fox One or NFL+ Premium. Currently, users can bundle ESPN Unlimited and Fox One for $39.99 per month, or ESPN Unlimited and NFL+ Premium for the same price.

ESPN’s decision to raise the price of its direct-to-consumer offering falls in line with the steady price increases of other streaming offerings. Most recently, Peacock bumped its monthly price up for the fourth time in four years, with the streamer’s base plan now running $12.99 per month.

Those who access ESPN through a cable, satellite, or virtual pay-TV bundle likely receive ESPN Unlimited at no additional cost. The network formally rolled out authentication to two of the largest pay-TV distributors in the country, Comcast and YouTube TV, earlier this year.

But for those outside the bundle, ESPN Unlimited will simply be the latest in a long line of streamers to raise prices.

# ESPN's streaming plans are getting more expensive: Here's what you'll pay

Bundles including Disney Plus and Hulu are also affected.

By Taylor Kerns

Aug 24, 2026 — 2:09 PM ET

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

TL;DR

- ESPN streaming plans and bundles are increasing in price.
- Plans are increasing by $1 to $3 per month.
- Adjustments also affect many streaming bundles that include ESPN.

Last week, we learned that Verizon will soon increase the prices for its Disney Plus, ESPN, and Hulu perks, with plan add-ons increasing by a buck or two per month starting in September. Now, ESPN has announced that its streaming subscriptions and the bundles they’re included in will be going up in price for everyone, not just Verizon subscribers.

As we’ve learned from 9to5Mac, ESPN has announced price hikes for its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited streaming plans. Select is increasing from $13 to $14 per month (or $140 per year, up from $130), while Unlimited is jumping from $30 to $32 per month (or $320 per year, from $300). Bundles including ESPN along with Disney Plus and Hulu are going up, too.

The bundle including Disney Plus and Hulu with ads along with the ESPN Select plan will cost $22 per month, up from $20. The version that includes ad-free Disney and Hulu streaming with ESPN Select will increase from $30 to $33 per month. Pricing is even going up for subscribers with the legacy version of that second plan, which is no longer available for new customers: it’s increasing $25 to $28 per month.

Prices for streaming services have been on the rise lately. Spotify, Netflix, Peacock, Apple Music, and more have raised fees this year, in tandem with steadily increasing sticker prices on hardware from smartphones to game consoles (and pretty much everything else, for that matter).

There is a slight silver lining in the case of ESPN Unlimited in particular, at least for some subscribers. While standalone ESPN Unlimited subscriptions are increasing in price next month, bundles including Unlimited won’t be affected by this round of price hikes. These changes take effect starting on September 17.

## There are some ways to keep streaming everything on ESPN Unlimited at no extra cost.

Danica Creahan, Liz Kocan

Thu, September 17, 2026 at 7:57 PM UTC

View larger image

Here's how to save a few bucks and avoid the new ESPN price increases. (Choreograph (Konstantin Yuganov) via Getty Images)

ESPN Unlimited is ESPN's premium streaming tier, which launched in 2025. Initially, the service cost subscribers $29.99/month (or $299.99/year) for access to all of ESPN's linear networks, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SECN, ACCN, ESPNews and ESPN Deportes, plus access to programming on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+ and ACCNX. A less-expensive option, ESPN Select, which is essentially a more robust version of the old ESPN+, also launched, costing $12.99/month.

But as is customary with all streaming services, those initial rates weren't going to last forever, and this week, ESPN announced that its Unlimited plan price has increased to $31.99/month, or $319.99/year, and the Select plan is now $13.99/month, or $139.99/year.

While we do love the fact that an ESPN Unlimited plan provides access to thousands of live events and other original programming, all of these increases take a toll on the old wallet. Fortunately, there are a few ways to make things hurt a little less. ESPN Unlimited is actually included in the price of several live TV streaming services like Fubo and DirecTV, cable providers like Spectrum, or you can bundle it with other platforms like FOX One to save big on monthly fees.

Here are some of the best ways to avoid ESPN's new price increases or get the plan for free!

DIRECTV offers several packages at all different price tiers, but if you want to get ESPN Unlimited included in one of them, you'll need to sign up for either their Choice, Ultimate or Premier packages (see all the plan descriptions and offerings here). Prices start at $64.99/month for your first month, and you'll also get unlimited Cloud DVR storage and access to Disney+, Hulu (with ads) included in each of these plans.

If you're a sports fanatic with little use for news or entertainment channels, DIRECTV's MySports Genre Pack costs even less, just $44.99 for your first 6 months, and it includes ESPN Unlimited along with 20+ additional sports channels. You can also try out any plan for free for five days.

### Save with a Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundle

### Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Unlimited 

We're fans of the Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Unlimited bundle; even though it's pricey at $35.99/month, it's a must-have for its vast array of sports and entertainment offerings, and even though ESPN just raised their subscription rates, the cost of the bundle hasn't increased.

(Football fans, take note: You can also add a subscription to NFL+ Premium to the bundle and pay $45.99/month. That's a $5/month savings, considering that a standalone NFL+ Premium subscription costs $14.99/month. A subscription to NFL+ Premium gets you live local & primetime regular season and postseason games on your phone or tablet, access to the NFL Network, live out-of-market preseason games, live game audio for every game, plus NFL Red Zone, NFL Pro, and full game replays.)

### Save with an ESPN Unlimited/FOX One bundle

#### ESPN/Fox One

That means subscribers can get coverage of more than 47,000 live events each year, on-demand replays, original programming and more. Purchased alone, the plan costs $31.99/month.

FOX One is the home to all the major FOX channels: FOX News, FOX Sports, FOX Weather, FS1, FS2, FOX Business, FOX Deportes, Big Ten Network (B1G), local FOX stations and FOX Network. Users also have access to on-demand content from FOX Entertainment, including movies, TV shows, comedies, ad-
